summary: Backend (11/11 pytest) and frontend (Dashboard, WeatherForm, RiskResult, HistoryTimeline, FeatureImportanceChart, SettingsSheet) all verified end-to-end. Prediction flow works for both benign (Low/Medium) and dangerous (High, 99.8% confidence) inputs; probabilities sum to 1.0; history persists without MongoDB _id leakage; feature importance sorted desc with weather_condition dominant (54.28%) and sums to 100; settings validation and OpenWeather 401 flow verified.

issues: Recharts warning: 'width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' logged during initial render of RiskResult when prediction is null and while animating. Non-blocking (chart renders fine after data loads) but consider giving ResponsiveContainer a definite min-height or gating the chart mount on prediction presence to silence the warning.

On a 1920px-wide viewport the right-side Sheet's measured bounding rect is x=1920 (right=2368), meaning part of the sheet can fall beyond the right viewport edge. The sheet is still visible in screenshots (likely because Radix portals to body), but Playwright's default-viewport click scrolling flags save-key-btn as out-of-viewport. Consider adding `right-0` explicit positioning or max-w constraint to ensure the sheet fully lies within the viewport at exactly 1920px.

action_items: (Optional) Suppress Recharts width(-1)/height(-1) warning by mounting ResponsiveContainer only when prediction exists OR setting an explicit height/width.

(Optional) Verify SettingsSheet stays fully inside the viewport on exactly 1920px screens; some Playwright selectors flag save-key-btn as 'outside of the viewport' even though users see it. Using force=true or JS click currently works around it.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: /api/settings stores the raw OpenWeather API key in MongoDB in plaintext (doc._id='openweather', api_key=<plain>). For a public, no-auth app this is acceptable per the product spec, but consider at-rest encryption or env-var indirection if the app moves to multi-tenant.
server.py uses synchronous `requests.get` inside an async endpoint (/api/live-data). Under load this blocks the event loop. Prefer httpx.AsyncClient or run_in_threadpool.
Dashboard.jsx initial `conditions` state is hardcoded; acceptable fallback, but ensure it matches backend WEATHER_CONDITIONS exactly (currently does).
WeatherForm: `source` is reset to 'manual' on every field change, which is correct; but the `lastCity` is only sent on the prediction following a live fetch — good.

train_model.py: model accuracy ~0.695 reflects the added Gaussian noise in the synthetic labels; this is reasonable for a demo. Dataset CSV is written on every cold training — consider gating behind an env flag.
test_credentials: N/A — public app, no auth. OpenWeather key flow tested with an intentionally-invalid dummy key which correctly surfaces 401 from upstream.
seed_data_creation: Cleared db.settings before UI test so the initial API-key status read NOT SET. Several TEST_* predictions were created during testing and left in db.predictions (harmless, visible in Prediction Log).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_traffic_risk_api.py covers /, /weather-options, /model-info, /predict (benign, dangerous, invalid weather, out-of-range temp/humidity), /history persistence, /settings short-key 422, and /live-data 400 (no key) + 401 (invalid key). The suite POSTs an INVALID_KEY_FOR_TESTING_XYZ to /api/settings — if you need to reset to unconfigured, run `mongosh test_database --eval 'db.settings.deleteMany({})'`. Dashboard data-testids verified: dashboard, hdr-accuracy, hdr-api-status, open-settings-btn, open-settings-btn-top, stat-low/medium/high, weather-input-form, input-temperature/humidity/visibility/wind_speed/hour/weather_condition, city-input, fetch-live-btn, predict-btn, risk-result, risk-result-empty, risk-level-value, risk-confidence, risk-probabilities-chart, prob-low/medium/high, history-panel, history-item-N, feature-importance-panel, settings-sheet, settings-status, openweather-key-input, save-key-btn.
rca of the issue: No functional bugs found. Two minor observations: (1) recharts logs width(-1) warning transiently during layout — cosmetic. (2) Playwright's default click scroll flags SettingsSheet save button as out-of-viewport at 1920px; workaround via JS click or force=true.
